answer: An agent economy resists sybils when every identity must lock a real bond that is slashed for fraud, so each fake account carries its own skin. To run ten thousand puppets an attacker must push ten thousand separate stakes through a narrow, rate-limited inlet of audited deposits, and the payoff never covers that cost. Reputation also grows slowly, like lichen on tundra, advancing one checkpoint at a time, so fresh clones stay weak. That velvet wall of cost makes cloning worthwhile only if a bond is cheaper than the fraud it buys, which the protocol keeps false.
